components.cost_effect: Two actual component p-jet calls per sampled residual; snapshot Taylor correction incurs no additional unknown-function query.
components.goal: Control recursive gradient error through pth-order snapshot subtraction.
components.key_estimate: Source Lemma A.1: E_i||Y_i||^2<=sigma^2, sigma=L_p m^(p-1)r^p/(p-1)!. Source Lemma A.2: error e_t=v_t-grad F(x_t), initialized at zero, is a vector martingale over performed updates with conditional increment second moment <=sigma^2/B. Zero-padding early termination gives terminal second moment <=m sigma^2/B and P(max_t||e_t||>sigma | epoch-start history)<=m/B<=1/64 when B>=64m. These are source-linked estimator statements, not a convergence theorem for this component.
components.name: Predictable same-index endpoint residual
components.operation: Let Y_i(x,s;z)=grad f_i(x+s)-grad f_i(x)-grad P_i(x+s)+grad P_i(x). Add its fresh uniform batch mean to v and add the exact polynomial-gradient increment.
components.requires: Stored snapshot p-jets, predictable endpoint pair and iid uniform fresh batch conditional on complete history; step and snapshot-distance bounds as above.
transfer_checks: Re-establish the residual second moment under changed smoothness or sampling.
Keep both endpoints at the same component index and account for both calls.
Maintain full-history fresh sampling after selecting the next point.
Supply the separate verified-epoch wrapper before invoking the paper's end-to-end optimization rate.

limitations.statement: This estimator does not generate the point path, solve the model, verify objective decrease or certify stationarity. No full-method rate is attached as a component performance link.
The recorded estimates are precise imported Lemmas A.1–A.2 from the selected PDF, not a separately extracted or independently re-proved theorem in this batch.

variants.cost: Initialization costs n complete component calls. Each uncached batch update costs 2B complete component calls, two endpoints for every sampled index. Polynomial evaluation and contractions use stored coefficients without new oracle calls. A full endpoint verification in Algorithm 1 costs an additional n calls and is not performed by this isolated component.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Section 4 equation (9), pp.6–7; Appendix A equations (15)–(22), pp.12–13.
variants.name: Fresh uniform Taylor-residual update
variants.output: Updated vector v_(t+1) estimating grad F(x_(t+1)), with cached P_i and P. No stationary point is certified by this output alone.
public_inputs: n>=1, integer p>=2, snapshot z in R^d, positive integer batch B and finite update horizon
Predictable next points x_(t+1)=x_t+s_t selected before the fresh batch
For the source epoch estimate: L_p, step bound r and epoch length m
variants.query_and_update: At an update, first choose s_t and x_(t+1)=x_t+s_t from existing information. Draw fresh I_(t,1),...,I_(t,B) iid uniform in [n]. For every b make two real component calls, at (I_(t,b),x_t) and (I_(t,b),x_(t+1)). Set v_(t+1)=v_t+grad P(x_(t+1))-grad P(x_t)+B^(-1)sum_b[grad f_(I_(t,b))(x_(t+1))-grad f_(I_(t,b))(x_t)-grad P_(I_(t,b))(x_(t+1))+grad P_(I_(t,b))(x_t)]. Retain the snapshot polynomials and new state.
variants.requirements: Exact scalar component value and derivatives through order p. For the source second-moment estimate, f_i in C^p(R^d) and [n^(-1)sum_i||D^p f_i(x)-D^p f_i(y)||_op^2]^(1/2)<=L_p||x-y|| for every x,y. Fresh batch indices are iid uniform with replacement, independent of the entire pre-draw history after the next point is chosen.
variants.state_and_initialization: At z query all n complete p-jets. Store P_i(y)=sum_{j=0}^p D^j f_i(z)[(y-z)^tensor j]/j! and P=n^(-1)sum_i P_i. Set x_0=z and v_0=grad F(z), exactly available from that pass.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: The component stops at its caller-supplied horizon or predictable early-stop decision. For Lemmas A.1–A.2 use at most m steps, ||s_t||<=r, ||x_t-z||<=(m-1)r at performed updates and B>=64m. Algorithm 1 uses m=ceil(sqrt(n)), B=64m and omits the final unnecessary estimator update. Its model-step selection and exact acceptance/termination wrapper are external to this component.

use_restrictions: Component specification and scoped source-linked estimates only; no independent end-to-end stationarity guarantee.
Fresh indices do not make oracle values stochastic: each indexed component is a fixed deterministic function.

research_use.reason: Subtracts stored high-order Taylor polynomials before recursive gradient tracking; unlike generic SPIDER tracking, the residual bound derives from pth-derivative increments.

source_refs.locator: Section 4 equation (9), Algorithm 1; Appendix A Lemmas A.1–A.2 and equations (15)–(22), pp.12–13

summary: Stores complete component p-jets at a snapshot and recursively estimates only the gradient residual using fresh uniform same-index endpoint pairs. This component alone has no end-to-end optimization complexity guarantee.
title: Snapshot Taylor-residual recursive gradient component
use_when: Reuse a snapshot polynomial while tracking gradients under mean-squared pth-derivative increments.
